items.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I would say mostly it was recordings of large orchestras, such as Paul Whiteman and the Benson Orchestra of Chicago.

ctx.x: Can you recall, as a child, what the first kinds of music that made an impression on you were?

Well when I was quite young, well I would go back probably to my grade school years, the first thing I remember musically is my mother used to work at a music store and she sold sheet music and records. And during that time she brought home a lot of samples, like old recordings — these would date back into the twenties. And that’s the first thing I remember is having this wind-up victrola in the home. It was considered a console model, where you put the record on the top and the sound came out the bottom through…

anything to anybody nowadays, and Charlie Straight was another orchestra that I listened to. And I became acquainted with the dance orchestras of the time by just playing these records. And of course at that time I wasn’t particularly — my mind wasn’t directed toward jazz at any particular amount at that time, and I was just becoming acquainted with music. I did it by records.
